topIssues.title: flake: TestPreserveDatabaseOnCLResync, TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync, TestCLUnsafeNotRewoundOnInvalidDuringELSync — stale engine RPC address after restart
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
## Flaky Tests

Three acceptance tests fail intermittently with the same root cause:

- `TestPreserveDatabaseOnCLResync` (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_clsync`)
- `TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync` (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_elsync`)
- `TestCLUnsafeNotRewoundOnInvalidDuringELSync` (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/sync/elsync/gap_clp2p`)

## Error

All three fail with:
```
failed to init L2: failed to setup L2 execution-engine RPC client: operation failed permanently after 10 attempts: address unavailable (ws://127.0.0.1:XXXXX)
```

## CI Link

https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/120052/workflows/55144005-177e-4fa8-b83e-0b782d8828e2/jobs/4629972/tests

Job: `memory-all-opn-op-geth` (4629972)

## Root Cause Analysis

All three tests follow the same pattern: stop L2EL (op-geth) + L2CL (op-node), then restart both. The issue is:

1. **Op-geth restarts on a new port** — `l2_el_opgeth.go` uses port `0` for engine RPC, so the OS assigns a fresh port each time. The TCP proxy upstream is correctly updated.
2. **Op-node reuses the stale config** — `singlechain_build.go:350` captures `l2EL.EngineRPC()` once at initialization. When op-node restarts in `l2_cl_opnode.go:68`, it reuses the same config with the old engine address.
3. **Op-node tries to dial the old port** — which no longer exists, fails after 10 retries.

### Why flaky, not consistent

The op-geth proxy address (`n.authRPC`) is set once and reused. If the proxy itself stays alive across the restart, the address remains valid. But when the proxy or geth is fully torn down and recreated, the downstream port changes while the op-node config doesn't update.

### Fix direction

In `l2_cl_opnode.go`, refresh the engine address from `l2EL.EngineRPC()` before creating a new op-node instance on restart, rather than reusing the stale config.

topIssues.title: fix(op-service/eth): Blob.UnmarshalText uses wrong hexutil label (Bytes32)
topIssues.author: cuiweixie
topIssues.body:
## Problem

`(*Blob).UnmarshalText` calls `hexutil.UnmarshalFixedText` with `"Bytes32"` even though `Blob` is a large fixed-size type (EIP-4844 blob), not 32 bytes. Error messages and validation can mislead callers.

## Expected

Use a type name consistent with `Blob`, e.g. `"Blob"`.

## PR

Tracked in the linked pull request.

topIssues.title: Flaky test: TestSuperCannonStepWithPreimage_nonExistingPreimage — challenger steps without uploading preimage
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
## Summary

`TestSuperCannonStepWithPreimage_nonExistingPreimage` (blob and sha256 subtests, mt-cannon-next) flakes regularly on CI. The test passes on retry, so it doesn't show up in failed test dashboards — but each failure wastes ~31 minutes before the retry succeeds in ~11 minutes.

## Root Cause (from CI log analysis)

**The challenger calls `step` without first uploading the required preimage to the oracle.**

From the CI logs (job 4726261, develop pipeline 121607):

1. **23:39:23** — Challenger logs `Invalid prestate` error:
   ```
   ERROR Invalid prestate  err="failed to validate prestate: super-cannon-kona absolute prestate does not match:
     Provider: 0x030ad443...093a506e | Contract: 0x035ef680...ae5d7c52"
   ```

2. **23:39:23 → 23:45:32** — Despite the prestate mismatch, the challenger continues: runs kona, generates proofs, makes bisection moves (claims grow from initial to 74).

3. **23:45:32** — Challenger reaches max depth and calls step:
   ```
   Performing action  action=step is_attack=true parent=73
     containsOracleData=false isLocalPreimage=false
   ```

4. **23:45:35** — Step transaction is confirmed onchain (`response_count=22`, `claims=74`).

5. **23:45:35 → 00:05:29** — Challenger loops doing nothing for **20 minutes**:
   ```
   Game info  claims=74 status="In Progress"
   Created preimage challenge transactions  count=0
   ```
   The preimage is never uploaded. The test's `WaitForPreimageInOracle` times out with `context deadline exceeded`.

## Key Questions

- Why does the challenger submit `containsOracleData=false` for a step that requires a preimage? Is the `Invalid prestate` error causing it to misidentify the oracle data requirements?
- The prestate mismatch (`Provider: 0x030ad4... | Contract: 0x035ef6...`) may be a race condition during test setup — on retry (fewer parallel tests), the prestates may align correctly.
- The step succeeds onchain but without the preimage data, so the oracle never gets populated.

## CI Evidence

| Run | Subtests Failed | Failure Duration | Retry Duration |
|-----|----------------|-----------------|----------------|
| Pipeline 121607 (job 4726261) | blob + sha256 | 31.1 min each | 11.2 min each |
| Pipeline 121550 (job 4725077) | blob only | 34.9 min | 11.3 min |

Full challenger logs available in the `testlogs.tar.gz` artifact:
- `testlogs/TestSuperCannonStepWithPreimagenonExistingPreimageblobmtcannonnext-31082.log`

## Test Location

- `op-e2e/faultproofs/super_test.go:234` — `TestSuperCannonStepWithPreimage_nonExistingPreimage`
- `op-e2e/e2eutils/disputegame/super_cannon_helper.go:101` — `ChallengeToPreimageLoad`
- `op-e2e/e2eutils/disputegame/cannon_helper.go:114` — `WaitForPreimageInOracle` (20 min timeout)

topPRs.title: feat(ops): add shadow CI system for dependency-aware test selection
topPRs.author: smartcontracts
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds a complete shadow CI system (`ops/shadow-ci/`) that runs alongside existing CI to prove equivalence before replacing it.

- **Language adapters**: Go (`go list`), Solidity (import parsing + remappings), Rust (`cargo metadata`) — build dependency graphs to compute affected targets from changed files
- **Core engine**: AffectedComputer, Planner, Executor (with retry + classification), Fingerprinter, ComparisonEngine — orchestrates dependency-aware test selection and proves catch rate
- **Platform adapter**: CircleCI renderer (TestPlan → YAML), results fetcher (artifacts → junit XML parsing)
- **Event store**: NDJSON-based unified event store with 20+ event types covering every decision point
- **Aggregator**: Weekly reports (catch rate, false negatives, speedup, top flakes) and dashboard data
- **Agents**: FlakeInvestigator, GraphMaintainer, ConfigVerifier, ReportAnalyst — autonomous remediation
- **6 CLI tools**: `affected`, `planner`, `render`, `runner`, `compare`, `aggregate`
- **Config-driven activation**: shadow → belt-and-suspenders → primary, controlled by `scoping.yaml`

### Key design decisions

- **Observability-first**: Every component emits structured events. Catch rate, false negatives, flake rate, skip rate, compute reduction — all derived from events.
- **Safety by default**: Starts in shadow mode (no gate on PRs). Belt-and-suspenders mode runs both systems and blocks if they disagree. Primary mode only after proven equivalence.
- **Self-healing**: False negatives automatically trigger graph gap detection and always-run list additions.
- **51 files, ~5,400 lines** of Go with own `go.mod` — zero dependencies on monorepo Go code.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./...` — 24 tests pass across 7 packages
- [x] `go vet ./...` — clean
- [x] `go build ./...` — clean
- [x] BFS graph traversal tests (diamond, linear, isolated)
- [x] Classifier tests (all classification combinations)
- [x] Fingerprinter stability tests (timestamps, IPs, ports normalize correctly)
- [x] Comparison engine tests (catch rate, false negatives, flake detection)
- [x] Event store tests (emit/query, type filtering, time filtering, persistence)
- [x] Solidity import parser tests (remappings, file collection)
- [x] Config loader tests (full YAML round-trip)

topPRs.title: feat(op-reth): Proof store v2
topPRs.author: dhyaniarun1993
topPRs.body:
**Description**

This PR introduces MdbxProofsStorageV2, an alternate MDBX backend for the op-proofs subsystem that replaces the v1 versioned-value schema with `3-table-per-domain pattern` (current state + changeset + sharded history bitmap).

**Motivation**

The proof storage ExEx has two sync paths:
- Fast path: block updates arrive in real-time from the ExEx notification stream and are persisted directly.
- Slow path: used during catch-up, where the node re-executes blocks and recalculates state roots to reconstruct the proof data.

The primary motivation is improving slow-path throughput. One of the bottleneck in the slow path is state root calculation, which requires reading the current state of every modified trie node and account. In the v1 schema these are stored as versioned DupSort entries — reading the latest value requires seeking past all prior versions. Under v2, the current state table holds exactly one row per key, so every read during state root computation is a direct O(1) lookup, eliminating the version scan entirely.

**Tests**

`tests/lib.rs` and `tests/live.rs` refactored to `#[test_case]` parameterised tests — each scenario runs against inmemory, mdbx (v1), and mdbxv2 backends from a single test body.

Devstack: `op-reth-with-proof-v2` EL kind
`op-devstack/sysgo/mixed_runtime.go` and `tests/proofs/utils/preset.go` support a new `MixedL2ELOpRethV2` kind so integration tests can target the v2 backend via `OP_DEVSTACK_PROOF_VALIDATOR_EL=op-reth-with-proof-v2`.


**Metadata**

Blocked on https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19909
